metadata.note: The Dunkirk and Fredonia street railway -- three miles down Central Avenue between the lake port of Dunkirk and the village of Fredonia, and the first trolley of any kind in Chautauqua County when it opened, horse drawn, in 1866. It was still a horse line when the 1881 county atlas noted only that Dunkirk 'is connected by a street line with Fredonia village'. Electrified as the Dunkirk & Fredonia Railroad in 1891, it lost its powerhouse and its cars to fire in 1900 and fell back on the old horse-cars for a few weeks until a temporary powerhouse and second-hand cars could be found. Its real significance is what grew out of it: this little street railway was the earliest predecessor of the Buffalo & Lake Erie Traction Company, which by 1909 ran 92 miles of interurban along the lake from Buffalo to Erie. The consolidation came in 1906, reorganisation as the Buffalo & Erie Railway in early 1925, and abandonment of the last remnants by 1935. Not to be confused with the steam road in dunkirk_allegheny_valley_pittsburgh_railroad.geojson, which ran inland from the same port.
sources: https://dunkirkhistoricalmuseum.org/history-of-dunkirk/ (Dunkirk Historical Museum): 'The first trolley, horse drawn, was established between Dunkirk and Fredonia, a first in the county' in 1866.

http://dunkirkhistoricalmuseum.org/research/bush-chronology/1900-to-1910/ (Dunkirk Historical Museum, Bush chronology): in 1900 'the electric railway between Dunkirk and Fredonia suffered a great loss when its powerhouse and cars were burned. Old horse-cars were used for a few weeks until a temporary powerhouse and second-hand cars could be obtained'; in 1906 'all the trolley lines between Buffalo and Erie were consolidated into the Buffalo & Lake Erie Traction Co., with a capital stock of $6,750,000'; in 1908 the Dunkirk Street Railway Company's belt line was completed and later that year became part of the Buffalo & Lake Erie Traction Company.

https://www.american-rails.com/nywintstrecrs.html (the B&LET was one of the state's largest interurbans, running about 92 miles along Lake Erie between Buffalo and Erie; 'the earliest predecessor of the company dated back to the Dunkirk & Fredonia Railroad of 1891'; the B&LE did not complete its main line until 1909; reorganised in early 1925 as the Buffalo & Erie Railway; the final remnants were abandoned by 1935. The 1900 American Street Railway manual lists the Dunkirk & Fredonia Railroad among owners of Briggs cars.)

https://chautauqua.nygenweb.net/HISTORY/1881ChautauquaCountyAtlas/HistoriesTranscriptions/DUNKIRK.htm (1881 Chautauqua County Atlas, Dunkirk: the village 'is connected by a street line with Fredonia village').
metadata.not_yet_sourced: The exact date the Dunkirk-Fredonia cars stopped running: the Buffalo & Erie system's last remnants went by 1935, but no last-car date specific to this line was found, so the final segment simply ends at 1935. Also unsourced: the electrification date beyond the 1891 incorporation, the precise streets used at each end (the route is drawn along Central Avenue, which an 1910 photograph of a trolley at Fourth Street and Central Avenue supports, but the exact downtown Dunkirk and Fredonia village terminal loops are not known), the Dunkirk Street Railway's 1908 belt line, and all frequencies.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API, routed over the ROAD network rather than the rail network: this street railway's track has been gone since the 1930s and OSM carries no trace of it, so the line is drawn along the streets it ran in -- Central Avenue between Dunkirk and the Fredonia village square. Both legs routed cleanly on real streets, no straight-line approximations.
Traced length 4.94 km, against the roughly 3 miles (4.8 km) the sources describe between the two villages.
Per-leg tracing result: ok Dunkirk (lakefront) -> Central Ave: 2 pts, 0.27km vs 0.25km crow (snap 10/19m) | ok Central Ave -> Fredonia (village square): 4 pts, 4.67km vs 4.56km crow (snap 19/8m)
metadata.horsecar_audit: 2026-08-24: removed as part of a repo-wide horsecar audit. Removed here: whole feature df-horsecar (whole feature; the 1866-1891 horse-drawn line, Chautauqua County's first). REPO RULE 5: this map shows MECHANICALLY powered rail -- horsecars and mule cars are out of scope, and a line's drawn years must start when it stopped using animals. Notes may still mention the animal era as context. See CLAUDE.md.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.interurban_audit: 2026-08-24: features on this layer that are inter-city electric railways were retagged mode='interurban' (previously 'streetcar' or 'intercity_rail') so the map can draw them distinctly from city streetcars and from steam roads. See CLAUDE.md Rule 7.
